title: The absolute mass scale of neutrinos
bottleneck: Oscillation experiments measure only differences of squared neutrino masses, leaving the absolute scale unknown anywhere below about 0.8 eV from tritium beta-decay endpoint measurements. Cosmology constrains the sum of masses but with model-dependent assumptions about dark energy and the early universe.
why_it_blocks: Neutrino mass is the only confirmed beyond-Standard-Model physics in particle physics; pinning its absolute scale determines the energy scale of the new physics that generates it, from eV-scale mechanisms to grand-unified seesaws.
current_state: KATRIN is pushing the tritium endpoint limit toward 0.2 eV sensitivity, while next-generation cosmological surveys aim to detect the summed mass through its imprint on large-scale structure. Project 8 aims to measure the tritium endpoint with cyclotron radiation spectroscopy, potentially reaching sensitivities that cosmology cannot match.
